newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, pushed down by Kolinska.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, pushed down by Kolinska.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.68 percent on Monday, pulled down by food producer Kolinska after the group listed a batch of new shares.
The SBI index fell 8.94 points to 1,307.62 and traders said the key index could fall to about 1,250 points by the end of the week unless new investors appeared on the horizon.
"Without fresh investment, the index could fall by about 50 points by the end of the week," said one.
Kolinska, which listed 650,977 new shares, fell 3.54 percent to 1,910 tolars on volume of 6,744.
But traders pointed out most listed shares could be a profitable long-term investment due to the current low prices.
"Practically all listed shares could be recommended for an investment period of over a year because at the moment prices are quite low," said Jasna Zontar, a trader at Modra Hisa.
He said mineral water producer Radenska, bank SKB and drug firm Lek could prove especially profitable.

Overall eight shares fell, six rose, two were unchanged and 11 were untraded, while one was traded for the first time. Turnover rose to 83.5 million tolars from 30.9 million, mainly on account of newly listed petrol trader Petrol.

Petrol, which is among the five largest companies in the country but is not yet included in the blue-chip index, was most actively traded, ending the day at 17,140 tolars after opening at 18,000, on volume of 1,987 shares.

Traders said Petrol's share price fall was largely due to a sell-off by small shareholders who bought the firm's shares in exchange for privatisation vouchers during Petrol's privatisation that ended last year.
"In the worst scenario Petrol could drop to 16,500 tolars while its current maximum seems to be at about 18,000 tolars," an analyst said.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, down 4.14 percent to 6,710 on volume of two shares only.
Bank UBK was the top gainer, closing 1.79 percent higher at 5,700 on volume of 29 shares. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
